meta.title: T02 impact, erosion and protection estimates (research, not canon)

V1_as_drawn.description: V1 geometry, canon forward shield only, nothing on the engine side

V1_skirt.description: V1 with the shadow-cone skirt (engine-first residual = bore-visible engine hardware)

CANON_skirt.description: canon ship with the flat aft skirt

notes: 120 keV protons stop within ~1 um of a surface (implantation, not penetration)
neutral H (~75 % of the LIC gas by number) cannot be deflected magnetically without first being ionised
blistering thresholds for H in metals are ~1e17-1e18 H/cm2 (EXTRAPOLATION from fusion-materials data; S-T02-BLISTER)

detection.assumptions: 1 J, 1.064 um pulse, 10 urad beam, albedo 0.1, 1 m2 receiver; vaporisation 1e7 J/kg; grain density 2500 kg/m3 (ASSUMPTION)
detection.search_rate_note: covering a 112 m radius at 100 km needs ~(112/0.5)^2 = 5e4 beam spots per 21 ms frame: ~2.4e6 pulses/s
detection.verdict: Grains are detectable only at ranges giving milliseconds of warning, and no beam can vaporise or deflect them in that time; the only workable 'clearing' is a physical screen that turns each grain into plasma far enough ahead (the stand-off physics above).

plume.model: steady conical plume, column from the exit plane to infinity on the axis; the grain meets plume ions at ve + v; pulsed bursts (FDP-1 pellets at ~100-200 Hz) are diluted by the same geometry
plume.verdict: The plume can vaporise grains below ~1e-15 kg; their vapour keeps its momentum and energy (momentum ratio < 1e-6). It removes far less than 1 % of the hazardous (> 1 ug) fluence. No credit.

V0.burn_solid_angle: zero for a point source (the sheet contains the burn's rays) and inside the shadow shield's umbra if set at or below the hardware cone; finite-source and scatter terms UNKNOWN (needs T04 source size)
